events.summary: Over the past week, we have expanded the suburb, added new ways to explore and destroy the environment, improved companion controls, and updated the bunker interface. More room to explore The suburb now has new accessible interiors in houses, trailers, shops, and other buildings. We have refined doors, stairs, and loot search points. events.title: Hunger, thirst, fatigue, and happiness are connected
events.summary: Hunger, thirst, fatigue, and happiness are connected The bunker slows down not because a timer decided to punish the player, but because people are exhausted. Food, water, health, and rest affect happiness, which changes work, recovery, and movement speed. A new room or successful return can lift morale; hunger, injuries, and broken equipment drag it down. Which status would you put on the main screen first?

events.title: Bunker residents do not wait for the cursor
events.summary: Bunker residents do not wait for the cursor A survivor who is hungry, wounded, and under orders should not behave like furniture. Priorities run from critical survival to direct orders, repair, normal needs, queued work, and self-development. An idle resident can train, rest, or help the bunker without a separate click. Do you prefer full control or autonomous residents with readable priorities?

events.title: A personal quest reveals a weakness, not a profession
events.summary: A personal quest reveals a weakness, not a profession A medic’s personal quest should be more than a trip for medicine. A personal storyline should expose fear, guilt, or contradiction. Afterward, bunker scenes, relationships, services, or restrictions change — the world notices the outcome. Whose story would you pursue first: Emily, Marcos, or Liam?

events.title: Reputation remembers how you spoke
events.summary: Reputation remembers how you spoke Characters remember more than completed missions — they remember who you were in conversation. Reputation influences dialogue options, personal quests, and relationship development. There is no marker for the “correct” line: you learn a person through behavior and past reactions. Are you willing to live with an imperfect answer without reloading?

events.title: Eight response tones, and no universally good button
events.summary: Eight response tones, and no universally good button The same kind of response can build trust with one person and shut another down. Dialogue uses eight tones: care, pragmatism, directness, humor, principle, caution, dare, and openness. Characters react according to personality, not a simple good-or-evil scale. Which tone do you choose most often?

events.title: Every survivor brings value and a cost
events.summary: Every survivor brings value and a cost A new person in the bunker is not just plus one population. Survivors have professions, skills, weaknesses, needs, and their own views of the System. They may improve a room, open a personal story — or bring a new conflict. Who do you take in first: a medic, an engineer, or a fighter?

events.title: Liam O’Connor: the rescuer who always goes first
events.summary: Liam O’Connor: the rescuer who always goes first When someone calls for help, Liam is already moving — usually before there is a plan. Before the catastrophe he was a firefighter; in the bunker he supports construction and heavy work. He values care for others and bold action, but can mistake caution for cowardice. Do you stop Liam, or run after him?

events.title: Marcos Rodriguez: discipline and dry humor
events.summary: Marcos Rodriguez: discipline and dry humor Marcos can joke under fire, but he will never forgive a plan with no exit route. A former soldier and survival instructor, he supports security and team training. He respects directness and dry humor, but rejects coddling and reckless dares. What convinces him faster: a clear order or a reckless “we’ll make it”?

events.title: Emily Rivers: healing others while avoiding her own pain
events.summary: Emily Rivers: healing others while avoiding her own pain Emily always asks, “Are you hurt?” before she asks what you brought back. She was a nurse and became the group’s medical anchor, but carrying everyone else’s pain pushes her toward burnout. Emily values care and openness, while cold calculation and badly timed jokes feel cruel to her. Would you admit your fear to her or try to break the tension with a joke?

events.title: Nathan Cole: the engineer looking for the source of the catastrophe
events.summary: Nathan Cole: the engineer looking for the source of the catastrophe Nathan helped build a safe AGI. Now he lives in a world where every answer about artificial intelligence sounds like an accusation. Before the catastrophe, he was an engineer and systems architect on Project Phoenix X. Now he must understand the System, keep people alive, and decide who can be trusted at all. If your own project stood beside the end of the world, would you defend it or suspect it first?

events.title: You hear gunfire behind a wall.
events.summary: You hear gunfire behind a wall. It could be a chance to help people — or a perfectly placed trap. Events trigger directly in the location and ask the player to act within a specific area and time. It may be a firefight, an escort, or a supply signal that turns out to be real — or bait. Do you investigate the gunfire or protect your route to extraction?

events.title: A secret rewards attention, not mandatory grinding
events.summary: A secret rewards attention, not mandatory grinding A crack in the wall should spark curiosity, not hide a mandatory path to victory. Secrets may be weak walls, psi illusions, suspended containers, fleeing rare enemies, or physical puzzles. The reward should feel good without turning secret hunting into mandatory optimization every run. What kind of secret would pull you away from a safe route?

events.title: Seven damage types, seven reasons to adapt
events.summary: Seven damage types, seven reasons to adapt If one damage type solves everything, a build stops being a choice. — The canonical set includes physical, fire, ice, electric, poison, psi, and mental damage.— Enemy resistances push the player to change weapons, utilities, and abilities for the situation. Which damage type do you bring into an unknown fight first?

events.title: An implant changes the build
events.summary: An implant changes the build An implant should change a decision, not just raise a number by one percent. — Implants are installed and replaced in the operating room as part of persistent character preparation.— An implant matters through its interaction with weapons, psi, and the character’s role. Would you build a flexible generalist or a narrow specialist?
